title: While I Lived Without the Lord
description: While I Lived Without the Lord in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 55, “Freedom from care”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: While I lived with-out the Lord, (If I might be said to live) Noth-ing could re-lief af-ford, Noth-ing sat-is-fac-tion give.

lines: While I lived without the Lord,
(If I might be said to live)
Nothing could relief afford,
Nothing satisfaction give.
Empty hopes and groundless fear,
Moved by turns my anxious mind;
Like a feather in the air,
Made the sport of every wind.
Now, I see, whate'er betide,
All is well if Christ be mine;
He has promised to provide,
I have only to resign.
When a sense of sin and thrall,
Forced me to the sinner's Friend;
He engaged to manage all,
By the way, and to the end.
"Cast, he said, on me thy care,
'Tis enough that I am nigh;
I will all thy burdens bear,
I will all thy wants supply.
Simply follow as I lead,
Do not reason but believe;
Call on me in time of need,
Thou shalt surely help receive."
Lord I would, I do, submit,
Gladly yield my all to thee;
What thy wisdom sees most fit,
Must be, surely, best for me.
Only when the way is rough,
And the coward flesh would start,
Let thy promise and thy love,
Cheer and animate my heart.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
